sun.declination_note: Southern-summer solstice: the Sun reaches the table's sun_elev_max_deg (5.04 deg) at local noon; the most sunlit season. Illustrative choice of season.
sun.window_note: Part of one lunar day (122 deg of hour angle, 10.0 Earth days): from shortly before the Sun clears the northern terrain to after it goes behind the western terrain. The rest of the cycle at this point is terrain shadow or night.

temperature_model.description: Stated shape model, not a measurement: T = Tmin + (Tmax - Tmin) * g, where g is the cycle-normalised value of a radiative-equilibrium shape (sin h)^(1/4) while the Sun is above the flat horizon AND more than half of its disc clears the real terrain horizon at the habitat, decaying after the last sunlit moment as g_sunset * exp(-t / tau). The curve is rescaled so that over the full cycle shown it reaches exactly the cell's measured Diviner minimum and maximum.
temperature_model.inset_tint: small inset only, blue (Tmin) to warm grey (Tmax)

earth_visibility.source: JPL Horizons API (DE441), observer at the site (coord@301, SITE_COORD 348.5 E, -86.5, 0 km), target 399, QUANTITIES=4, APPARENT=AIRLESS, 2026-01-01..2044-12-31 every 12 h (13,879 rows), queried 2026-11-15
earth_visibility.decision: Drawn at its 2026-2044 mean position (az 11.52, elev 3.14 deg) only if that is above the real terrain horizon in that direction; its monthly libration wander (az 3.5-19.7, elev -3.8..10.1 deg) is not animated.

habitat.assumption: Illustrative engineering shapes, not a real design: rigid cylindrical module 4.0 m diameter x 8.0 m long on its side; inflatable section 6.0 m diameter x 5.0 m long attached at one end; regolith berm 1.5 m high, ring of 11 m inner radius. Deployment order and timing are illustrative.

card.title: Earth analog and lunar twin: lunar base, analog 2 of the five shown
card.subtitle: Analog 2 of the five shown (overall rank 3). Suitability 43.15, similarity 97.31, final 70.23. The lunar cell lies in NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole. Values from the project tables (1-degree cells); each carries its level.
card.levels_source: variables.json variables[].bodies[EARTH|MOON].level; Moon coldest temperature MEASURED per missions.json missions[lunar_base].similarity.variables[tmin_k].sides.MOON (Diviner tmin_k); relative elevation DERIVED per missions.json elevation_rel_m sides
card.legend: Percentiles: the Earth point among the 2,419 Earth candidates of the Lunar base mission, the lunar cell among the 280 cells of the nine NASA regions. Earth coldest temperature: WorldClim 2.1 modelled air temperature of the coldest month (non-commercial licence); Moon: Diviner measured surface night minimum. They are not the same quantity. Relative elevation: elevation minus each body's mean.

render.lighting_note: Sun: one parallel light (the real low Sun, at most 5.04 deg up); terrain shadows from the real LOLA horizons; 3.5 % uniform fill standing in for light reflected by the surrounding sunlit ground (assumption). Display exposure (a camera setting, the light is not changed): 1 while the habitat site sees the whole solar disc, x16 while it sees none, and 1/(1/16 + (15/16) x visible disc fraction) in between; stated on screen whenever it is above 1.25.

en.header: Lunar base mission video (3D simulation), English descriptive captions
en.note: No speech. Each cue gives the values on the on-screen panel at its start time; the panel status does not change within a cue. The surface temperature follows a stated model curve between the cell's measured Diviner minimum (41.23 K) and maximum (194.51 K); the Sun is computed; habitat shapes, sizes and timing are illustrative. While the site is in shadow the display exposure is raised (not to scale).

text: 3D simulation driven by table data, not real footage. Lunar cell M63528, 86.5° S 11.5° W, 25.1 km from Mons Malapert, in NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole, over real LOLA relief. The camera descends to the site. The Sun is up but behind the northern terrain: the site is in shadow (exposure raised, not to scale).
The Sun rises over the northern terrain.
The cylindrical module is lowered onto its legs.
The module rests on the ground.
The inflatable section expands from the end of the module.
The inflatable section is deployed.
A regolith berm rises in a ring around the habitat.
The berm is complete.
The habitat is assembled. The Sun stays below about 5° and moves west, low over the terrain; shadows are very long.
The Sun starts to go behind the western terrain.
The Sun is behind the western terrain while still above the flat horizon: the site is in shadow and its surface cools. Exposure raised to show the ground (not to scale).
The site stays in shadow. At its mean position the Earth is hidden behind the terrain from here, so there is no earthshine.

Closing card: analog 2 of the five Lunar base analogs shown (overall rank 3; suitability 43.15, similarity 97.31, final 70.23). The Earth analog in Xinjiang Uygur Zizhiqu, China (cell E17538, 41.5° N 78.5° E) and its lunar twin, cell M63528 near Mons Malapert, paired by relative thermal position, not by equal temperatures. Coldest temperature 248.61 K (−24.54 °C, modelled air) against 41.23 K (−231.92 °C, measured surface), percentiles 8.37 and 8.04; daily swing 15.60 K against 153.27 K, percentiles 6.72 and 10.18; slope 6.652° against 7.179°; roughness 238.81 m against 238.49 m; mean temperature 272.06 K against 77.49 K (not part of the similarity).

This pair matches by relative thermal position, not by equal temperatures. In real values the twin is 195 K colder on average (minimum −232 °C at the surface against −24.5 °C air temperature here) and its day-night swing is 138 K larger; slope differs by 0.5° and roughness by 0.3 m. 3D simulation driven by table data. Not real footage.

es.header: Vídeo de la misión base lunar (simulación 3D), subtítulos descriptivos en español
es.note: Sin voz. Cada subtítulo da los valores del panel en pantalla al inicio del subtítulo; el estado del panel no cambia dentro de un subtítulo. La temperatura de la superficie sigue una curva de modelo declarada entre el mínimo (41,23 K) y el máximo (194,51 K) medidos por Diviner en la celda; el Sol es calculado; formas, tamaños y tiempos del hábitat son ilustrativos. Mientras el punto está en sombra se aumenta la exposición de la imagen (no a escala).

text: Simulación 3D basada en datos de las tablas, no son imágenes reales. Celda lunar M63528, 86,5° S 11,5° O, a 25,1 km de Mons Malapert, en las nueve regiones candidatas de alunizaje de la NASA cerca del polo sur lunar, sobre el relieve real LOLA. La cámara desciende hasta el punto. El Sol está sobre el horizonte pero tapado por el relieve del norte: el punto está en sombra (exposición aumentada, no a escala).
El Sol asoma sobre el relieve del norte.
El módulo cilíndrico se baja sobre sus patas.
El módulo queda apoyado en el suelo.
La sección inflable se expande desde el extremo del módulo.
La sección inflable está desplegada.
Un muro de regolito se levanta en anillo alrededor del hábitat.
El muro está terminado.
El hábitat está montado. El Sol no pasa de unos 5° y se desplaza al oeste a ras del relieve; las sombras son muy largas.
El Sol empieza a ocultarse tras el relieve del oeste.
El Sol está tras el relieve del oeste aunque sigue sobre el horizonte plano: el punto queda en sombra y su superficie se enfría. Exposición aumentada para mostrar el suelo (no a escala).
El punto sigue en sombra. En su posición media, la Tierra queda oculta tras el relieve desde aquí, así que no hay luz cenicienta.

Tarjeta final: análogo 2 de los cinco análogos de la base lunar mostrados (puesto 3 de la clasificación completa; idoneidad 43,15, similitud 97,31, final 70,23). El análogo terrestre en Xinjiang Uygur Zizhiqu, China (celda E17538, 41,5° N 78,5° E) y su gemela lunar, la celda M63528 cerca de Mons Malapert, emparejadas por posición térmica relativa, no por temperaturas iguales. Temperatura más fría 248,61 K (−24,54 °C, aire, modelada) frente a 41,23 K (−231,92 °C, superficie, medida), percentiles 8,37 y 8,04; oscilación diaria 15,60 K frente a 153,27 K, percentiles 6,72 y 10,18; pendiente 6,652° frente a 7,179°; rugosidad 238,81 m frente a 238,49 m; temperatura media 272,06 K frente a 77,49 K (no forma parte de la similitud).

Este par se parece por posición térmica relativa, no por temperaturas iguales. En valores reales la gemela es 195 K más fría de media (mínima −232 °C en la superficie frente a −24,5 °C de temperatura del aire aquí) y su oscilación entre el día y la noche es 138 K mayor; la pendiente difiere en 0,5° y la rugosidad en 0,3 m. Simulación 3D basada en datos de las tablas. No son imágenes reales.

captions.cue_rule: Cue boundaries are the frames where the panel status changes (render.js --timeline), plus 34.5 s and the closing card; render.js refuses to write captions if the status changes inside a cue.
